items.question: Roughly how much living and working volume did Skylab give its crews?
items.reference_answer: Over 10,000 cubic feet of living and experimental workspace.
evidence: cubic-feet of living and experimental workspace

items.question: How many docking ports was the Multiple Docking Adapter originally built with?
items.reference_answer: Five: one axial and four radial.
evidence: equipped with five docking ports, one axial and four radial

items.question: What made it possible to fit the workshop with an active food freezer?
items.reference_answer: Launching the workshop dry on a Saturn V gave more payload capability and more liberal weight allowances, so an active food freezer/chiller system could be added.
evidence: add an active food freezer/chiller system thereby enhancing the quality of food

items.question: How was drinking water stored in the Orbital Workshop?
items.reference_answer: In ten stainless steel tanks spaced around the forward compartment, each holding at least 600 pounds of usable water, with a metal bellows pressurised by nitrogen to push the water out.
evidence: consisted of ten stainless steel water tanks evenly spaced

items.question: What minimum iodine level was needed for the water to be safe to drink?
items.reference_answer: 0.5 ppm or more; the crew checked with a colour comparator that it stayed above 2 ppm.
evidence: iodine concentration was to have been 0.5 ppm or greater

items.question: What was the job of the cation cartridge in the water system?
items.reference_answer: It held ion exchange resin that removed metal ions from the water flowing through it.
evidence: remove metal ions from the water as it passed through the resin bed

items.question: What did the astronauts dislike most about the shower?
items.reference_answer: The power module: its low air flow made cleaning up the shower water take too long, so the whole procedure was too time consuming.
evidence: The primary complaint was the inadequacy of the power module

items.question: How many soap bars did the first crew actually get through?
items.reference_answer: Only one bar for the entire mission, although eleven were provided for it.
evidence: they used only one bar for the entire mission

items.question: Why did the crews go through more tissues than planned?
items.reference_answer: Because of nasal congestion in zero gravity; the third crew ran out in some dispensers and used utility wipes instead.
evidence: Due to zero-g nasal congestion

items.question: How did the crew stop the fabric louvres of the light baffles from collapsing?
items.reference_answer: They cut triangular pieces of cardboard, put them into the louvre stiffeners and taped them in place.
evidence: triangular shaped pieces of cardboard

items.question: What was the thermal sail made of?
items.reference_answer: Aluminized mylar coated with S-13G paint, as a 22 by 24 foot rectangle.
evidence: aluminized mylar coated with S-13g

items.question: In neutral buoyancy training, what stood in for the sail material and why?
items.reference_answer: Half-inch nylon netting, chosen to minimise drag while moving the sail through the water.
evidence: nylon netting

items.question: How long did engineers have to come up with the sail concept before the first crew launched?
items.reference_answer: Eleven days, from the discovery of the failures on the SL-1 launch day to the SL-2 launch on May 25.
evidence: In eleven days, from the discovery of the system failures

items.question: Which telescope was the focal plane camera designed for?
items.reference_answer: The 2.4 meter Space Telescope.
evidence: Focal Plane Camera for the 2.4 meter Space Telescope

items.question: Why does the camera include its own on-axis pick-off mirror?
items.reference_answer: The SECO detector and filter mechanism are too bulky to sit in the high-quality centre of the focal plane, so the mirror folds that central part to one side, leaving the other instruments access.
evidence: integral on-axis pick-off mirror to fold the central portion

items.question: Why was electronic exposure control preferred over a mechanical shutter?
items.reference_answer: Gating voltages in the detector avoids the reliability questions of a precision mechanical shutter.
evidence: preferable to the introduction of a precision mechanical shutter

items.question: How heavy is the focal plane camera and how much power does it use on average?
items.reference_answer: About 310 pounds, with an average power of 97 watts.
evidence: Weight - 310 Pounds

items.question: Why is the detector mounting bulkhead aluminium rather than invar?
items.reference_answer: The camera submodule is mounted to it, and aluminium gives a good heat conduction path away from the submodule.
evidence: made from aluminum and the camera submodule is actually mounted to this bulkhead

items.question: What working fluid is used in the camera's heat pipes?
items.reference_answer: Ammonia.
evidence: Working Fluid - ammonia

items.question: How many positions does each filter wheel have, and what turns it?
items.reference_answer: Eight positions per wheel, each wheel indexed by a stepper motor through a 200:1 reduction.
evidence: Each wheel has eight positions

items.question: How much can a moving filter wheel disturb the telescope's pointing?
items.reference_answer: Only marginally and momentarily: about 0.009 arcsecond of body pointing, plus about 0.004 arcsecond of vibration that damps out within seconds.
evidence: marginally-significant disturbance to the line-of-sight

items.question: What positions can the capping shutter be set to?
items.reference_answer: Three: open for imaging, open for standard star calibration, and closed for internal calibration.
evidence: thus has three positions

items.question: How does an astronaut secure the camera module once it is in place?
items.reference_answer: By tightening the four captive screws one after another with a ratchet wrench, after registration pins centre the module and latches hold it.
evidence: tightens the four screws successively with a ratchet wrench

items.question: How many levels of confidence does the IPCC's calibrated language distinguish?
items.reference_answer: Five: very low, low, medium, high and very high.
evidence: uses five qualifiers to express a level of confidence

items.question: What probability range does 'very likely' stand for in IPCC reports?
evidence: very likely 90–100%

items.question: What was the concentration of CO2 in the atmosphere in 2019?
items.reference_answer: 410 parts per million, higher than at any time in at least 2 million years.
evidence: atmospheric CO2 concentrations (410 parts per million)

items.question: How large were global net greenhouse gas emissions in 2019?
items.reference_answer: About 59 ± 6.6 GtCO2-eq, about 12% higher than in 2010 and 54% higher than in 1990.
evidence: 59 ± 6.6 GtCO2-eq

items.question: What share of household emissions comes from the highest-emitting 10% of households?
items.reference_answer: 34-45% of global consumption-based household GHG emissions, while the bottom 50% contribute 13-15%.
evidence: The 10% of households with the highest per capita emissions contribute 34–45%

items.question: How many people live in places that are highly vulnerable to climate change?
items.reference_answer: Approximately 3.3 to 3.6 billion people.
evidence: Approximately 3.3 to 3.6 billion people

items.question: About how many people face severe water scarcity for part of the year?
items.reference_answer: Roughly half of the world's population.
evidence: Roughly half of the world’s population currently experience severe water scarcity

items.question: What does the report mean by climate resilient development?
items.reference_answer: Development that integrates adaptation and mitigation to advance sustainable development for all.
evidence: Climate resilient development integrates adaptation and mitigation

history.content: What was wrong with the Skylab shower?
The main complaint was the weak power module: its low air flow made cleaning up the water take too long [1].

items.question: How much water did it use each time?
items.expected_standalone: How much water did one shower on Skylab use?
items.reference_answer: Six pounds per shower, which all crews found adequate.
evidence: six-pounds of water, per shower

history.content: What was used to purify Skylab's drinking water?
Iodine was used as a biocide in the water tanks [1].

items.question: What concentration were the tanks charged to at the start?
items.expected_standalone: To what iodine concentration were Skylab's water tanks initially charged?
items.reference_answer: 12 ppm, expected to fall to at most 6 ppm by the time the water was used.
evidence: initially charged with iodine until the concentration was 12-ppm

history.content: What was the twin pole sail on Skylab?
A thermal shield of coated mylar held out on two 55-foot poles to shade the workshop from the sun [1].

items.question: Who put it up, and on which mission?
items.expected_standalone: Who deployed Skylab's twin pole sail, and during which mission?
items.reference_answer: Two EVA crewmen (EV-1 and EV-2) installed it during the first EVA of SL-3.
evidence: installed during the first EVA of SL-3
accomplished by two crewmen

history.content: How is the focal plane camera's detector cooled?
Thermo-electric coolers cool the photocathode to 270 K [1].

items.question: Why does it need to be that cold?
items.expected_standalone: Why is the photocathode of the focal plane camera's detector cooled?
items.reference_answer: So that the camera has a wide dynamic range and a high signal-to-noise ratio at the video output.
evidence: wide dynamic range and high signal-to-noise ratio

history.content: Which lamps does the camera's internal calibration use?
A tungsten lamp and a high pressure hydrogen lamp [1].

items.question: How long does the second one last?
items.expected_standalone: How long does the high pressure hydrogen calibration lamp of the focal plane camera last?
items.reference_answer: Usually a few hundred hours.
evidence: The life of the lamp is usually a few hundred hours

history.content: How much has the world warmed according to the IPCC synthesis report?
Global surface temperature in 2011-2020 was about 1.1°C above 1850-1900 [1].

items.question: Was it more over land or over the sea?
items.expected_standalone: Was the warming in 2011-2020 larger over land or over the ocean?
items.reference_answer: Over land: about 1.59°C, against 0.88°C over the ocean.
evidence: larger increases over land

history.content: How fast is the sea level rising now?
The average rate reached 3.7 mm per year between 2006 and 2018 [1].

items.question: And how much has it gone up in total since 1901?
items.expected_standalone: How much did global mean sea level rise in total between 1901 and 2018?
evidence: Global mean sea level increased by 0.20

history.content: What does the IPCC report mean by the near term?

items.question: And the long term?
items.expected_standalone: How does the IPCC synthesis report define the long term?
items.reference_answer: The period beyond 2040.
evidence: The long term is defined as the period beyond 2040
